bihar_raw_news.title: Kacchi Dargah-Bidupur Bridge Set for Nov 21 Inauguration - Urban Acres
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News Kacchi Dargah-Bidupur Bridge Set for Nov 21 Inauguration Breaking News Kacchi Dargah-Bidupur Bridge Set for Nov 21 Inauguration By Urban Acres November 10, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp The 19-km Kacchi Dargah-Bidupur six-lane Ganga bridge will be inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi during his visit to Bihar on November 21, Bihar BJP president Sanjay Saraogi said at a joint press conference in Patna on Monday. The project is expected to strengthen the road link between Patna and Vaishali, reduce travel time and ease pressure on existing routes. The project comprises a 9-km main bridge across the Ganga along with approach roads, according to the report. Its inauguration will create a new north-south connection for Bihar, linking the Patna side at Kacchi Dargah with Bidupur in Vaishali district. Saraogi said the inauguration would be part of an official government programme and that National Democratic Alliance constituents would coordinate arrangements for the Prime Minister’s visit. The bridge is among the infrastructure projects being presented as part of the state government’s wider development programme covering roads, railways, air connectivity, power, healthcare and education. The new crossing is expected to provide an alternative route for movement between Patna and north Bihar. Existing connections across the Ganga carry traffic serving residential areas, commercial activity and regional movement, making the availability of an additional six-lane crossing significant for road connectivity. The report, however, does not provide an estimated reduction in travel time, traffic capacity figures or details of the operating and maintenance arrangements for the bridge. Modi is also scheduled to attend a programme at the Jafarpatti Industrial Area in Rajapakar block of Vaishali district during the visit. Saraogi said the programme would focus on industrial development, infrastructure expansion and employment opportunities. He said development of the industrial area could attract investment and create employment and entrepreneurship opportunities, particularly for young people. The visit is scheduled to coincide with the completion of one year of the National Democratic Alliance government in Bihar on November 20. Janata Dal (United) state president Umesh Singh Kushwaha described the visit as a matter of pride and said the development process initiated under Chief Minister Nitish Kumar was being carried forward by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary. Other alliance leaders also described the visit as an occasion to showcase development projects in the state. The bridge’s public significance will depend not only on its inauguration but also on how effectively its approaches connect with the surrounding road network and how traffic is distributed after opening. The supplied report does not specify the opening schedule for regular traffic, toll arrangements, final approach-road details or measures to manage traffic around the new corridor. The Prime Minister’s Bihar programme, including the scheduled inauguration of the Kacchi Dargah-Bidupur bridge and the event at Jafarpatti Industrial Area, is set for November 21, according to the announcement. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Free Power Subsidy Faces Rs 23,000-Crore Strain - Urban Acres
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News Bihar Free Power Subsidy Faces Rs 23,000-Crore Strain as ‘Give It Up’... Breaking News Bihar Free Power Subsidy Faces Rs 23,000-Crore Strain as ‘Give It Up’ Drive Begins By Urban Acres November 10, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Bihar will launch a ‘Give It Up’ campaign on December 1, urging affluent residents and income-tax payers to voluntarily forgo the 125 units of free electricity provided every month under the state’s subsidy scheme. Chief minister Samrat Choudhary said the move is intended to reduce the financial burden on the state exchequer while protecting the benefit for economically weaker households and needy consumers. The chief minister announced the campaign while speaking to reporters during a visit to a Mahadalit settlement on the Digha-Ashiana Road in Patna. He said the free-power initiative currently covers households across income groups and benefits around 1.92 crore families in Bihar. According to Choudhary, the electricity subsidy costs the state approximately Rs 23,000 crore annually. He put the average annual cost at nearly Rs 10,000 per family. The proposed campaign will ask financially better-off beneficiaries to voluntarily contribute towards the subsidy instead of continuing to claim the free-power benefit. “From Dec 1, we will launch a campaign encouraging those who wish to voluntarily contribute towards the electricity subsidy. Just as Prime Minister Narendra Modi appealed to people to voluntarily give up their LPG subsidies, we are making a similar appeal,” Choudhary said. The 125-unit free electricity facility is provided under the Mukhyamantri Vidyut Upbhokta Sahayata Yojana. The scheme was announced by former chief minister Nitish Kumar on July 17, 2025, and implemented across Bihar from August 1, 2025. Officials said the proposed ‘Give It Up’ campaign would remain voluntary. Free electricity of up to 125 units a month will continue for economically weaker sections and other needy consumers, according to the report. The government has not announced a compulsory income threshold or a detailed process for identifying consumers who may opt out. Officials also said that savings generated from affluent beneficiaries who voluntarily surrender the subsidy will be channelled directly into improving educational infrastructure and other development projects in the state. The announcement therefore links the electricity support programme to a broader question of how Bihar funds both household relief and public investment. The campaign follows the state government’s decision to extend the free-power benefit across Bihar rather than restrict it to a specific economic category. Its proposed voluntary structure means the immediate impact will depend on how many eligible consumers choose to give up the subsidy and how the government records and redirects the resulting savings. Choudhary made the announcement during a Diwali visit to underprivileged communities, where he distributed gifts and called on public representatives and administrative officers to celebrate the festival with Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe and Extremely Backward Class communities. The government’s next stated milestone is the launch of the ‘Give It Up’ drive on December 1. Share Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Previous article Chhath Special

national_raw_news.content: The Supreme Court has asked WhatsApp and other intermediaries to apprise it about their proposed measures to prevent digital arrest scams and related cybercrimes in the country. A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant asked WhatsApp and similar intermediaries to simultaneously submit their proposals to the I4C (Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre). The order regarding it uploaded on the website with regard to the hearing conducted on 29th of last month in a suo motu case titled ‘Victims of Digital Arrest Related to Forged Documents’, The bench, also comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, has listed the plea for further consideration on 23rd of this month. WhatsApp, had told the bench the platform had taken preventive measures, including action against 9,400 accounts, and would file an affidavit detailing the steps undertaken. The top court, on October 29, had said financial institutions must be held accountable for digital arrest scams and other cyber frauds, emphasising that banks should be required to compensate victims for losses suffered where an investigation establishes that the fraud occurred due to the institution’s failure to exercise due diligence. The bench also directed the law enforcement agencies of all states and Union territories to submit reports detailing FIRs registered in digital arrest scam cases and the investigations arising from them.

national_raw_news.title: President Murmu stresses people-centric policing, urges IPS officers to address public grievances
national_raw_news.content: President Droupadi Murmu has urged IPS officers to prioritise alleviating the fears of socially or economically weaker individuals who generally lack access to senior officials, and addressing their grievances. Addressing, Probationers of the 2025 batch of Indian Police Service today at Rashtrapati Bhava the President said for the citizens, police officers and constables are symbols of governance. She said, people perceive the governance to be good when the police system functions well. The President said that the People feel immensely supported when a police officer listens to their grievances with sensitivity and attentiveness. The President stated that some of the employees in the system may be more proficient in the use of technology than the senior officers. She advised the officer trainees to not hesitate to learn even from the most junior members of their team. She urged them to encourage public participation and teamwork in their working style. She said that by prioritising the welfare of their team members, they will enhance their capabilities and enthusiasm. The President said that the police officers would derive a high level of authority from the laws and rules related to policing. However, they will earn real respect from the people, based on their performance and value system. She said that they should have a sense of commitment to serving citizens rather than a sense of superiority over them. She highlighted the need for police officers to always stay ahead of the criminals who use state-of-the-art technologies.

national_raw_news.title: BCCI announces Smriti Mandhana led squads for upcoming all-format tour of South Africa 09 Nov 2026 | 8:00 PM 284
national_raw_news.content: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) Women’s Selection Committee has announced squads for the upcoming all-format tour of South Africa in December. Smriti Mandhana is set to lead the side across all three formats. India will play one Test, three ODIs and three T20Is during the tour, which will begin with the Test match in Gqeberha on 9th December. The ODI series will start on 16th December in Paarl, followed by the second match in Cape Town on 19th December and the third in Bloemfontein on 22nd December. The three-match T20I series will begin on December 26 in Benoni. The second and third matches are scheduled to be played in Potchefstroom. Deepti Sharma has been named vice-captain of the Test and ODI squads, while Shafali Verma will serve as vice-captain in the T20I format. The Test squad features 15 players, including Harmanpreet Kaur, Jemimah Rodrigues, Richa Ghosh, Yastika Bhatia, Sneh Rana and Kranti Gaud. The ODI squad also comprises 15 players, with Vaishnavi Sharma included in place of Sneh Rana from the Test squad. The T20I squad has 17 players, with Shafali Verma as vice-captain. Niki Prasad, G. Kamalini, Anushka Sharma, Prema Rawat, Amanjot Kaur, Renuka Singh Thakur and Arundhati Reddy are also part of the squad.

national_raw_news.title: Trump says his immigration policy ‘too tough’ after midterm drubbing
national_raw_news.content: US President Donald Trump acknowledged that his immigration policy was “too tough” after a severe drubbing in the midterm elections and said he was ready to work with the Democratic Party in the years ahead. Democrats won control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate in the November 3 midterm elections, flipping several Republican-held seats in a sweeping setback for Trump. The results reflected voter dissatisfaction with his handling of the immigration issue, the economy, the Iran war and rising living costs. “I think it was too tough. I think it might be too tough,” Trump told CBS’ 60 Minutes in response to a question on his administration’s deportation policy. The interview was recorded on Friday and telecast on Sunday evening. Soon after the interview was recorded, Trump appointed Stephen Miller, known for his strong views against immigration, as his Chief of Staff, raising questions about whether the President would significantly soften his approach. Asked about the reasons for Republicans’ resounding defeat, Trump echoed the conventional wisdom that it was due to the Iran war and gas prices, while also pointing to hostility towards Israel as a factor. “They didn’t like the war,” Trump said. “They didn’t like the fact that gasoline went up because I had it down at a low. And there’s a great dislike, incredibly, for Israel.” The President said his immigration crackdown had “both helped and hurt” him at the polls. Trump said he believed he “got an A+ for closing up the border” and “very high marks for getting the bad ones out”. “But I get hurt because we also took people that had good jobs, that created one violation, or breaking of the law, and that was that they came into the country illegally,” he said. “Now, there is a large part of the country that thinks that they should be put out. And there’s a large part of the country that thinks that they should be allowed to stay if they’re good people working in a landscaping company, or working in a hotel, or doing something, right? And in some cases, paying taxes. “I think it was too tough,” the Republican leader reiterated. Asked what he thought would happen after his death, Trump said, “I hope I’m missed.” He also described himself as a “religious person” and said he hoped to go to heaven. (PTI)

national_raw_news.title: Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 records sales of Rs 55.46 lakh at Dilli Haat, showcases artisans’ craftsmanship
national_raw_news.content: The ongoing Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 at Dilli Haat, INA, in the national capital, has recorded cumulative sales of approximately ₹55.46 lakh between November 1 and 8, reflecting strong public response and growing market opportunities for artisans from disadvantaged communities. Organised by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, the 15-day fair will continue until November 15. It provides a platform for artisans and beneficiaries belonging to Scheduled Castes (SCs), Other Backward Classes (OBCs), Safai Karamcharis and persons with disabilities to showcase and market their products to a wider audience. The sales were recorded by four participating corporations: the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC), National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC) and National Divyangjan Finance and Development Corporation (NDFDC). The Ministry has been organising Shilp Samagam Melas since 2022. Over the years, more than 1,000 artisans from SC, OBC and Safai Karamchari communities have benefited from opportunities to exhibit and sell their products. The initiative aims to promote self-employment, encourage entrepreneurship and support the socio-economic empowerment of beneficiary communities. Organised around the theme ‘प्रकाश और परंपरा – ज्योति से ज्योति जलाएँ’, the current edition features more than 130 stalls across seven thematic zones: कला आँगन, प्रकाश चौक, पूजा पथ, सजावट बाज़ार, घराना, स्वाद चौक and मंच. The exhibition showcases a wide range of handicrafts, handloom products, traditional textiles, festive decorations, lamps, home décor items and other indigenous creations. To help beneficiaries participate, the Ministry provides free stalls, travel expenses, daily allowances and transportation facilities for their goods. These measures are intended to reduce financial and logistical barriers and enable artisans to reach new customers and markets. The fair also promotes wider market access through initiatives such as Bharat TULIP, which connects artisans with e-commerce platforms, and Purple Fest, which highlights the creativity and capabilities of persons with disabilities while encouraging inclusion and equal opportunities. Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment Virendra Kumar, Minister of State Ramdas Athawale, Minister of State for Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution Nimuben Jayantibhai Bambhaniya, and Secretary of the Ministry Sudhansh Pant have visited the Mela. They toured the stalls, appreciated the craftsmanship and interacted with participating artisans, reiterating the government’s focus on inclusive entrepreneurship and sustainable livelihood opportunities. Cultural programmes held every evening at the Mela’s Manch are another major attraction. Artists and performers from different states present folk dances, traditional music and regional art forms, offering visitors an opportunity to experience India’s cultural diversity on a common platform. The fair has been drawing families, young visitors and other members of the public, who are exploring traditional products while supporting artisans and their efforts towards entrepreneurship, economic empowerment and self-reliance. (PIB)
